readerQuestionCoverage.item: How do I layer different skin acids?
readerQuestionCoverage.whyThisMatters: Layering low-pH and neutral-pH ingredients incorrectly neutralizes their efficacy or causes chemical burns.
readerQuestionCoverage.finalCopyUse: Introduce wait times and pH hierarchy (apply lowest pH acid first, wait 5-10 minutes, then apply neutral-pH barrier creams).

readerQuestionCoverage.item: Should oily skin double cleanse daily?
readerQuestionCoverage.whyThisMatters: Daily double cleansing removes sweat-resistant silicone sunscreen and metropolitan pollution.
readerQuestionCoverage.finalCopyUse: Explain that oily skin benefits from PM double cleansing with a gentle oil/balm and non-stripping gel cleanser.

recommendationSanityPlan.whyThisMatters: Azelaic acid is a dermatologist-favored gentle exfoliant that is safer for Fitzpatrick Types III-VI than high-dose glycolic acid.
recommendationSanityPlan.finalCopyUse: Detail standard concentration, suitability, and pharmacy pricing range for Indian users.

claimRiskPlan.item: Glycolic acid is the safest exfoliant for all Indian skin types
claimRiskPlan.whyThisMatters: High strength glycolic acid can trigger post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation on darker Fitzpatrick skin types.
claimRiskPlan.finalCopyUse: Soften the claim by advising low concentrations (5-8%) or lactic acid alternatives for sensitive brown skin.

troubleshootingPlan.whyThisMatters: Combining too many resurfacing acids ruins the lipid barrier.
troubleshootingPlan.finalCopyUse: Introduce a step-by-step troubleshooting protocol for peeling, stinging, or redness.
